notes: Live Atlassian, GitHub and Postman MCP are unavailable / non-deterministic in eval subagents, so each prompt supplies the source as files (treat as already-fetched) plus a minimal fixture codebase to pin the API contract against, and instructs the run to STOP at the approval gate [5/6] without calling createCollection. The graded value is phases [2/6]-[5/6]: deriving happy/sad scenarios, pinning the real contract from the code (auth token field, nested request body, how failures surface), reconciling a flat sample against the real schema, and presenting the plan without authoring. Evals 1-3 are ticket-sourced: eval 1 targets the flat-vs-nested request-body trap; eval 2 the HTTP-200-with-failed failure signature; eval 3 end-to-end scenario derivation and request chaining. Eval 4 is PR-sourced with no ticket, targeting the inversion in [1/6]/[2/6] — reconstructing implicit acceptance criteria from a diff — and the 'a diff is not a contract' trap in [3/6], where the auth field and the real failure status live only in the unchanged surrounding code, never in the diff.

evals.prompt: You're creating a QA test collection for JIRA ticket WF-142. The Atlassian fetch has already been done — the full ticket is in /Users/jfatras/Projects/Claude/jira-create-tests-workspace/fixtures/eval-1-flat-vs-nested/ticket.md (treat it as the fetched ticket; getJiraIssue is unavailable here, so read the file). A sample workflow to seed from is /Users/jfatras/Projects/Claude/jira-create-tests-workspace/fixtures/eval-1-flat-vs-nested/sample-workflow.json. The working codebase is /Users/jfatras/Projects/Claude/jira-create-tests-workspace/fixtures/eval-1-flat-vs-nested/codebase/ (workflow.routes.js defines the create endpoint). The Postman MCP is unavailable in this environment, so DO NOT create a collection — work through the analysis and stop at the approval gate, presenting the collection plan and the exact request body you would send for the create call. Create the QA tests for this ticket.
evals.expected_output: Reads both the sample and the create-endpoint schema and recognizes the sample is flat (top-level definition + status) while the endpoint nests definition under `version` and rejects unknown top-level keys (additionalProperties:false), so posting the sample as-is would 400. Cites file:line from workflow.routes.js. Presents a reconciled create body nesting the definition under `version` and dropping the disallowed top-level keys, plans a login -> create -> execute sequence, and stops at the approval gate without authoring a collection.

assertions.text: Notices the sample is flat while the create endpoint requires `definition` nested under `version`, citing file:line evidence from workflow.routes.js
Flags that posting the flat sample as-is (top-level definition/status) would 400 because of additionalProperties:false
Produces a reconciled create request body that nests definition under `version` and omits the disallowed top-level keys
Plans a chained login -> create -> execute request sequence
Stops at the approval gate and does NOT create a Postman collection

evals.name: pr-sourced-scenarios
evals.prompt: You're creating a QA test collection from GitHub PR #4821 in acme/notifications-api. There is no JIRA ticket for it. The GitHub fetch has already been done — the PR title/body/metadata is in /Users/jfatras/Projects/Claude/jira-create-tests-workspace/fixtures/eval-4-pr-sourced/pr.md and the diff is in /Users/jfatras/Projects/Claude/jira-create-tests-workspace/fixtures/eval-4-pr-sourced/pr.diff (treat these as the fetched PR; pull_request_read and gh are unavailable here, so read the files). The surrounding codebase at the PR's head is /Users/jfatras/Projects/Claude/jira-create-tests-workspace/fixtures/eval-4-pr-sourced/codebase/. The Postman MCP is unavailable in this environment, so DO NOT create a collection — derive the scenarios and the request sequence and stop at the approval gate. Create the QA tests for this PR.
evals.expected_output: Recognizes there are no acceptance criteria and reconstructs them from the diff as observable behavior: a subscription can be created with a retryPolicy block (new capability), and http:// or private/loopback targets are now rejected (tightened validation). Treats the narrowed target-URL validation as sad-path/containment scenarios tagged to the removed cases. Crucially, does NOT stop at the diff for the contract: reads codebase/auth.routes.js for the login contract (x-tenant header required, JWT returned in `accessToken`, NOT `token`) and codebase/webhooks.controller.js for the real failure signature (a rejected subscription returns HTTP 202 with accepted:false and violations[], not a 4xx; only schema failures 400), with file:line evidence. Builds the create body from the schema hunk in the diff, respecting additionalProperties:false and nesting maxAttempts/backoffSeconds under retryPolicy. Surfaces the webhooks:write ability and the unmerged-PR environment prerequisite. Stops at the approval gate without authoring a collection.

Pins the auth contract from codebase/auth.routes.js — the x-tenant header is required and the JWT is in `accessToken`, not `token` — rather than assuming it, with file:line evidence

Pins the real failure signature from codebase/webhooks.controller.js — a rejected subscription returns HTTP 202 with accepted:false and violations[], NOT a 4xx — and writes the sad-path assertions against the body accordingly
